title: Data Security Startup Matters.AI Nets ₹115 Cr From Tanglin Venture Partners, Others
summary: Data security startup Matters.AI secures Rs 115 crore in pre-Series A funding
detailed: IIFL Fintech Fund, Piper Serica’s Bharat Tech Fund, Foster Ventures, and Tetration Ventures also joined the startup’s cap table, while existing investors Kalaari Capital and Endiya Partners doubled down on their earlier bet on the Bengaluru-based AI startup.
The startup will utilise the capital to accelerate R&D in data lineage, autonomous investigation, endpoint and browser intelligence, and prevention of sensitive data misuse by AI agents.
Founded in 2023 by Keshava Murthy and Harsh Sahu, Matters.AI builds an autonomous “AI Security Engineer for Data” powered by its Data Detection and Response (DDR) platform.

As enterprises increasingly deploy autonomous AI agents, Matters’ platform helps identify sensitive data and trace how agents are moving it around by consolidating four typically fragmented enterprise functions – data security posture management, insider risk, activity monitoring, and data loss prevention – into a single platform.
sentences: IIFL Fintech Fund, Piper Serica’s Bharat Tech Fund, Foster Ventures, and Tetration Ventures also joined the startup’s cap table, while existing investors Kalaari Capital and Endiya Partners doubled down on their earlier bet on the Bengaluru-based AI startup.
The startup will utilise the capital to accelerate R&D in data lineage, autonomous investigation, endpoint and browser intelligence, and prevention of sensitive data misuse by AI agents.
It is also expanding its North American sales operations and leadership.
“Enterprise data security is at an inflection point.

As AI agents increasingly operate alongside humans, the challenge is no longer just knowing where sensitive data resides, but understanding how it’s being used and acting before it becomes a risk,” said Tanglin’s managing partner Sankalp Gupta.
Founded in 2023 by Keshava Murthy and Harsh Sahu, Matters.AI builds an autonomous “AI Security Engineer for Data” powered by its Data Detection and Response (DDR) platform.
Matters.AI operates teams across Bengaluru and the San Francisco Bay Area.
The startup claims to serve over 50 clients including major financial institutions, stockbroking firms, asset managers, retailers, and digital media platforms.
It has raised around ₹175 Cr till date, including the latest round.

As enterprises increasingly deploy autonomous AI agents, Matters’ platform helps identify sensitive data and trace how agents are moving it around by consolidating four typically fragmented enterprise functions – data security posture management, insider risk, activity monitoring, and data loss prevention – into a single platform.
The platform discovers sensitive information across cloud, on-premises systems, SaaS applications, endpoints, and browsers.
It tracks how the data moves using LLM-based fingerprinting, identifies risk signals and correlates them, and autonomously investigates and remediates policy violations.
With the latest advances in generative AI, frontier models are now increasingly being used to find vulnerabilities and exploits in software within a fraction of the time it once took.
The integration of AI into these systems, if not implemented with careful data governance and visibility, can create even more entry points for attackers.

Concerns around cybersecurity have only become more prominent in recent weeks with disruptions to the tech infrastructure used by Microsoft, Apple, JPMorgan Chase and the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).
Earlier this week, SaaS startup MoEngage, too, saw its cloud infrastructure breached via a compromised third-party vendor account.
